title: Write-batch result (D3g)
description: The JSON a write subagent prints on stdout for an apply-* or implement batch. It is the batch's `output_path` (apply_batch_N.json / implement_batch_<task id>.json), validated exactly like a validation result before anything is written — a runner that returns prose fails the task instead of being counted as applied (D3f). It is NOT the verdict: the executor's own pre-batch snapshot / post-run byte comparison decides applied vs. clean failure vs. partial application, and `summary` is the field `prior_changes.py append` takes its one-liner from, which is why it is part of the contract rather than a nicety.

status.description: The runner's own claim. `applied` = it edited files; `no-op` = nothing needed changing (already applied by a prior batch); `failed` = it could not apply the batch. Never the verdict on its own: a claim of `applied` with an empty snapshot diff is a clean failure, and a claim of `failed` with a non-empty diff is a partial application.

ids.description: The suggestion/group/task ids this batch actually applied. Compared against the task's `expected_ids` so 'some of them landed' is detected as a partial application rather than read as success.

files_touched.description: The files the runner says it edited, repo-root-relative. Cross-checked against the observed diff; the observed set — not this one — is what the write policy is enforced against post-run.

summary.description: One line, <= 200 chars. Goes verbatim into `prior_changes.py append --summary`, which is why the contract requires it: the injected prior-batch context must come from a structured field, never from compressing a chat reply.

notes.description: Optional free-text detail for the batch report and the implementation summary. Never parsed.

usage.description: Optional runner-reported usage. Absent means NOT REPORTED, never zero (D3j); the executor records duration itself either way and never derives token counts.

check.description: A check task's structured result (an implement task that declares no files), and since fix round 14 a code batch's report of the checks it ran on its own edits (implement's tasks that declare files, apply-code-fixes' batches): the contract asks for it only there. Optional, so an older reply stays valid. On a code batch, `passed: false` or any `findings` entry records the batch applied with a failing check — never a plain success, and never a hold (`subagent_executor.batch_check_findings`; a `check` that says neither is no report there). On a check task: `passed: false` or any `findings` entry records the task `check-findings` instead of `verified`: no file changed, the tasks that do not depend on it go on, the tasks that do are not run, and the findings reach summary.md, the reports, `status` and review-code (racing re-run 4, 2026-10-05; fix round 11). Read from this field, never from `notes`. No `type` here or below on purpose (fix round 11): a near-miss shape (`passed: "false"`, `findings: "one problem"`, a number as a finding, `check: {}`) used to fail the reply's validation, and implement has no report re-ask, so the run stopped for good. `subagent_executor.check_findings_from` reads every shape instead, and only a clear pass with nothing listed is a pass; `check: null` is an unknown result, not a missing one (fix round 12).

passed.description: true only when every check the task names ran and met its acceptance criteria. Read leniently (true/false, 1/0, "true"/"false"); anything else is an unknown result, never a pass.

could_not_run.description: true when a check the task names could not run (its command missing, a crash, a timeout, no result printed); the reply is then `failed` and the task stops implement, whatever `findings` lists. Read leniently (true, 1, "true", "yes"). Without it a `failed` reply whose `findings` lists problems is recorded `check-findings`, as a check that ran (fix round 12: runners answer `failed` for a check that ran and failed).

findings.description: One string per problem a check reported; empty when passed is true. A check that could not run is not a finding: the reply is `failed` with `could_not_run: true`. An object is read as its values, a bare string or number as one finding — except a bare "none", "n/a", "no problems found", "" or 0 beside a passed that reads true, which is no finding (fix round 12).
